_comment: Every item the quest puts in the player's hands. Becomes TweakXL records in
the same loose r6/tweaks/ash_cache.yaml as the character records - one file,
because TweakXL reads a directory and a rename that split them would let the
graph grant an item nothing defines.
Two shapes, both taken from shipping mods rather than invented:
kind 'item'   Lucy's Dedra_LucyEncryptedCoordinates: inherit a vanilla item
with $base and override the name. Two lines. For things the
player carries but never opens.
kind 'shard'  Aldecaldos High Stakes' sq_hs_regina_shard: a full
gamedataItem_Record with itemType Gen_Readable, a Readable tag
and an inline gamedataItemAction_Record whose journalEntry
points at an onscreen entry holding the text. Vanilla's own
mq006_body_shard has exactly this pair of records, so the
mod shape is the game's shape.
Every 'base' is verified to exist in the game's TweakDB by tools/validate.py
(D11), as is the absence of every 'record' - a record name that already exists
would overwrite a vanilla item rather than add one.
A shard's text lives in source/strings.json like all other text and is
delivered as an onscreen journal entry, which is why it gets a title AND a
body: the title is the shard's header in the UI, the body is the read view.

_casting: The quest object. Three of the four endings are literally 'do something
with the splinter', so it has to be a thing in the inventory rather than a
fact - and a thing the player cannot lose.
q003_chip is the Flathead from The Pickup: the game's own plot MacGuffin.
Reading its record is what settled this. It is Gen_Misc, ItemCategory.General,
isSingleInstance, tagged 'Quest', and its objectActions list contains NEITHER
Drop NOR Disassemble - so the player cannot throw the plot away.
The first draft of this file used Items.MilitechJunkItem3, copied from Lucy's
mod. That record is ItemType.Gen_Junk, tagged Junk, and carries
ItemAction.JunkDisassemble - one 'disassemble all junk' click and the quest
object is gone. Fine for Lucy's collectible; wrong for this.
D119. What the terminal download actually hands over. Before it, the
terminal beat set a fact and nothing else - the player pressed Use, the
objective ticked, and the records the objective is ABOUT were never seen.
A shard rather than a plain item because the text is the point: kind
'shard' is the pair of records that gives an item a Readable action and
an onscreen journal entry, so this one can be opened and read like any
shard in the game, in either locale, forever after.
Mara hands this over in the Hide ending only (OI-1 - she has to be alive
to do it). Same base as the splinter, for the same reason: it is a quest
object, not loot, and it must not be droppable or sellable.
Items.q001_secret_room_keycard looked like the obvious pick and is not: its
tags are empty and its objectActions are Drop + Disassemble, so it is an
ordinary carryable that happens to be named after a quest.
D121. The only thing Mara ever physically hands over on the three routes
where V does not tell her to get lost, and the answer to a question the
scene could not answer before: why does she stand there while Hale's crew
shoots the place up? Because she is an analyst who has drawn a gun twice in
nine years, she knows it, and she says so while giving it to someone who
will do better with it. Her not fighting stops being an engine limitation
and becomes the character.
The Liberty is Militech's federal sidearm - what a NUSA agent is issued.
Casting it as HERS is the whole joke: nine years undercover carrying the
one object that would have identified her instantly.
The FIRST item in this file that is a weapon rather than a quest object, so
it is also the first whose displayName override has to survive a weapon
record's own name resolution. If the override does not stick in game it
degrades to an ordinary Liberty - a working pistol with the wrong name, not
a broken grant. Worth an eyeball in the inventory.
Deliberately NOT undroppable, unlike the splinter and the master key. Those
are the plot; this is a present. A present the player is not allowed to
sell is a debt.

tweak: tags: [Weapon, RangedWeapon, OneHandedRangedWeapon, DriverCombatRangedWeapon, DriverCombatBikeWeapon, PowerWeapon, Preload, Handgun, Liberty, IconicWeapon]
_casting: D186. The Liberty on the ground beside her body, made a real pickup: a trophy.
Only on the routes where she had a gun (ashcache_mara_liberty_given), same as
the prop it replaces. AshCacheTrophy.reds drops it as a vanilla loot item once V
is near her and the glue's visual prop goes away on the same fact.
Built like Dex's Plan B (Preset_Liberty_Dex, read live 2026-09-26): the iconic
blueprint, the IconicWeapon tag, IconicQualityRandomization in place of the
random-quality and random-mod groups, Quality.IconicItem in statModifiers. It
keeps the DEFAULT visualTags so it looks like the gun that was lying there.
keep_actions: an iconic is a present too - droppable, not a quest object.
The stat numbers are repeated in item_mara_trophy_desc; change both.
D122. Two records, one shard. Exactly one is ever granted: the graph picks
on ashcache_mara_liberty_given at the moment V reaches the body, so a save
can never hold both and the player can never see the other ending's wound.
They share displayName, description and shard title on purpose - same case,
same clerk, same four closing words - so that the ONLY thing that differs
between two playthroughs is the one paragraph that says how she died. A
player who compares two saves is meant to find that paragraph and nothing
else.
The hostile route's copy. V told her to get lost, so there was no Liberty
to recover and her forearms took the defensive wounds instead. See the
sibling record above for why the two are identical everywhere else.
D129. The only thing V comes away from the shaft head with, and the whole
payload of the aftermath objective - there is no prop and no interaction,
because the fiction is that the way down is already welded shut.
It also does the reconciling. Voss says on the phone that the dig runs
under the Badlands; the game's own geometry puts the outer bunker under
Dogtown, with the motel inside its footprint. This plate says both are
true on paper, which turns a contradiction into the reason nobody has
checked the archive in four years.
D131. What the shaft head is worth to a player who jacks the maintenance
port instead of just prying the plate off - and the first description of
Cynosure as a place rather than a word: nine levels, which ones are
flooded, where the archive is and what is priority-1 powered.
Two lines in it do the work. The pumps log a maintenance cycle every
eleven days on a facility that was shut four years ago, and the cold
store is short exactly one item - 0-1140, which is the number stencilled
on the splinter already in the player's inventory (see hud_absorb_top).
The carrier who signed it out never signed out at grade, because he got
as far as a motel wall 250 m above this plate.
